notes.title: Amazing demo release and future updates!
notes.notes:
It's been 3 weeks and I'd like to share my thoughts on how the demo release went

[h2]Surprising Demo Reception[/h2]
The demo launch of "All in your head" went far beyond my expectations, I couldn't have ever imagined so many people playing it. It's been heartwarming to see so many of you immersing yourselves in the eerie world I've created and noticing the subtle hints I've left here and there for the eagle-eyed. I'm truly thankful to all the streamers and YouTubers who played the game, created content, and shared it with their communities.

[h2]The Jumpscares[/h2]
I'm delighted to report that the three jumpscares in the game worked as intended, spooking players and catching them off guard, just as I had hoped. Creating those suspenseful moments was an essential part of my vision for why I started all this in the first place.

[center][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41962637/0c45b2fee709153cea82fdcbe5e078a1f1da783b.gif[/img][/center]
[i]Fun fact: This jumpscare was the first thing I created when I started the project in Unity[/i]

[h2]1000+ new wishlists![/h2]
In just three weeks, we've gathered more than a thousand new wishlists for AIYH. Your support means the world to me, and it inspires me to work even harder to deliver the best horror gaming experience. We're going strong!

[h2]Thorough Bug Fixing[/h2]
Your feedback has been invaluable, and I've been diligently addressing any issues and glitches noticed during Let's Play sessions. Some of the bugs we've tackled include flashlight glitches, Japanese subtitles not displaying correctly, problems with clicking, and adjustments to mouse sensitivity.

[h2]Unexpected Steam Next Fest Success[/h2]
Participating in the Steam Next Fest been the best decision I've made so far w.r.t. to the development cycle. It not only got me motivated enough to start working more regularly on the game but the visibility it got was insane - drawing a much much larger audience. Your enthusiasm played a significant role in this exciting outcome.

[center][h1]Future Updates[/h1][/center]
[h3]Expanded Story[/h3]
There's more to Miley's story that will be included in the full game. You can expect a deeper, more immersive narrative experience as you progress through the game.

[h3]Work in Progress[/h3]
While the demo was just 2 out of 8 acts, there's still much work I need to do for the full game. The remaining acts are in development, and I'm dedicated to delivering a complete and compelling horror adventure.

[h3]Feedback Improvements[/h3]
I still have a lot of feedback to work on, such as showing objectives on the pause menu, implementing a better hint system because many players forgot the codes or were distracted when they were shown, and enhancing the use of Tab and Esc keys.

[center][h1]A Heartfelt Thank You[/h1][/center]

I can't thank you all enough for your continued support, feedback, and enthusiasm. Your involvement has been instrumental in making All in your head better. I'm committed to delivering a horror game that will provide a truly chilling experience.

Thank you for being a part of this incredible journey. Stay tuned for more updates as we progress towards the full release of All in your head.

[h2]Got feedback?[/h2]
I'm always looking for more feedback here on [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1830770/discussions/1/]steam[/url], [url=https://discord.gg/S8MpSbnE]AIYH Discord[/url], [url=https://twitter.com/UsamaIndieDev]twitter[/url] or any other place for that matter!

[h2]Haven't played the demo yet?[/h2]
No worries, the demo is live, free to play and I don't plan on taking it down.

[h2]Watch playthroughs[/h2]
Watch my own [url=https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLMM2G99Z48dYOl4VBwenhUXqHOWFAK5zV&si=S6qg_5jPbE3v19eI]Youtube Playlist for All in your head Let's plays[/url]. It would be great if you check these people out and like their videos on Youtube!

notes.title: Development Update
notes.notes:
For the past 2 weeks, I’ve been working on making the cut scene – the first one, which would introduce the first part of the story to the player. What I’ve learned is that it’s much harder than I thought.

[b]My assumptions before starting[/b]

I thought that since I have experience with animations and key framing, I would have ease going through the cutscene animations. After all, I have rigged characters ready to animate, all I need is a reference footage and I can start animating! Spoiler alert -> I was wrong. So very wrong.

[b]Characters[/b]

Even if you have rigged characters, you might not have what you need. There are countless amounts of different rigs that different engines use to animate a character. E.g. Some characters might have 25 bones on their face just to control their expressions, others might just have 1 head bone because they don’t require facial expressions. They might be okay with just the head movement

[b]3d Software[/b]

It took me 2 weeks just to get comfortable with Blender – an open source 3d software that many indies like myself use for animations, modelling and sculpting etc. The community is amazing and supportive, I had tonnes of people volunteering to help out. A special shout out to fudgenuggets87 whose great advice on reddit encouraged me to start learning blender.

[b]Reference Footage[/b]

Note to self -> It’s impossible to record your own video from an orthographic view rather than a perspective view. It’s impossible to align your own reference footage with the animation because there will be no amount of angles that you can use to compensate for the fact that your camera has only 1 lens. And if you don’t use a reference footage, you risk animating your characters a little too cartoonish. Here’s what I mean:


Trying to sync the movement with my reference footage.
Note how the feet and arms are not aligned fully because of the perspective of the camera
So where am I now?

Finally, now I am fluent enough with Blender to produce an acceptable animation. But still, it takes me 3 hours to do about 15-20 seconds right. Having said that, All in your head game will not have more than 3 3 or 4 minutes of animated cutscenes. So I think we’re good for as far as the timeline is concerned.

Here’s a sneak peak of the new features of the level. What do you think?


As always, feel free to comment your feedback, email me or [url=www.twitter.com/usamaindiedev]follow me on twitter[/url]. Thanks for reading, I’ll see you in the next one.
